answer: Each identity claims one bridge span, locks an 80-credit bond, and files a violet tag bound to that span and epoch. A midspan test load drops the deck against a fixed horizon sight line in the registry. An auditor recomputes the drop from span length and the load table: a reading over 3 percent off or a reused violet tag burns the bond. The k-th fake costs 41+5(k-1); the 1,000th costs 5,036, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,538,500 plus 80,000 locked bonds. A rented-gauge ring fails: one serial in two filings voids both bonds. An honest identity pays 41 once and keeps its bond after a clean epoch.
